textContent: Zoological Garden Alipore The Zoological Garden Alipore, popularly known as Alipore Zoo, is India’s oldest officially established zoological park and one of Kolkata’s most visited tourist attractions. Spread across nearly 46.5 acres (18.8 hectares) in the heart of Alipore, the zoo attracts millions of visitors every year, especially during the winter months. Established in 1876, the zoo is home to hundreds of species of mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fish from India and around the world. It has played a significant role in wildlife conservation, education, captive breeding, and public awareness for nearly 150 years. Whether you are travelling with children, nature enthusiasts, wildlife photographers, or first-time visitors to Kolkata, the Zoological Garden Alipore offers an enjoyable and educational experience. History of Zoological Garden Alipore The idea of establishing a zoological garden in Kolkata emerged during the British colonial period. The project gained momentum under the guidance of Richard Temple, the then Lieutenant Governor of Bengal, and naturalist Ram Brahma Sanyal, who became the zoo’s first superintendent. The zoo officially opened to the public on 1 January 1876, making it the oldest formal zoological garden in India. Throughout its long history, the zoo has introduced numerous conservation initiatives and breeding programs for endangered species. Perhaps its most famous resident was Adwaita, the Aldabra giant tortoise, believed to have lived for over 250 years. Adwaita became one of the oldest known tortoises in the world and remained one of the zoo’s biggest attractions until his death in 2006. Architecture and Layout Unlike modern theme-based zoological parks, the Zoological Garden Alipore combines colonial-era landscaping with spacious animal enclosures, shaded walking paths, water bodies, and lush gardens. Major sections include: Mammal Enclosures Reptile House Aquarium Aviaries Butterfly Garden Waterfowl Lake Nocturnal Animal Section Herbivore Zones Big Cat Enclosures Large trees, ornamental gardens, and scenic lakes make the zoo pleasant even for visitors who simply enjoy walking through nature. Animals at Zoological Garden Alipore The zoo houses a wide variety of wildlife from across India and several international species. Big Cats The biggest crowd pullers include: Royal Bengal Tiger White Tiger African Lion Leopard Jaguar (when on display) Bears Visitors can observe: Sloth Bear Himalayan Black Bear Primates Popular primates include: Chimpanzee Baboon Rhesus Macaque Langur Herbivores The zoo features: Giraffe Zebra Hippopotamus Rhinoceros Nilgai Blackbuck Sambar Deer Spotted Deer Reptiles The reptile section includes: Indian Python King Cobra Crocodile Gharial Monitor Lizard Turtles Tortoises Birds Bird lovers can enjoy: Macaws Hornbills Pelicans Flamingos Emus Ostriches Peacocks Parrots Eagles Owls Conservation and Breeding Programs The Zoological Garden Alipore participates in several national conservation initiatives. Some important breeding successes include: White Tigers Asiatic Lions Indian Rhinoceros Gharials Various endangered birds The zoo collaborates with wildlife authorities to promote scientific breeding and conservation of threatened species. Best Time to Visit The ideal time to visit is between October and March, when Kolkata experiences pleasant weather. Winter mornings are especially comfortable, and many animals tend to be more active. Avoid visiting during: Hot summer afternoons Peak holiday rush if you prefer fewer crowds Weekdays are generally less crowded than weekends. How Much Time Should You Spend? Most visitors spend between 2 and 4 hours exploring the zoo. Families with children often spend longer enjoying the various exhibits. How to Reach Zoological Garden Alipore By Metro The nearest metro stations include: Majerhat (Purple Line) Jatin Das Park (Blue Line) Auto-rickshaws and taxis are readily available from these stations. By Bus Several city buses connect Alipore with: Esplanade Howrah Garia Salt Lake Behala By Taxi App-based cabs and traditional taxis can easily reach the zoo from anywhere in Kolkata. Approximate travel time: Esplanade: 20–30 minutes Howrah Station: 35–45 minutes Sealdah Station: 35–45 minutes Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport: 60–90 minutes (traffic dependent) Nearby Attractions Visitors often combine the Zoological Garden Alipore with other attractions nearby: National Library of India Victoria Memorial St. Paul’s Cathedral Maidan Alipore Museum Race Course Birla Planetarium Visitor Tips Visit early in the morning for the best animal sightings. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Carry drinking water, especially during warmer months. Follow all zoo rules and avoid feeding the animals. Maintain silence around animal enclosures. Keep the premises clean by using designated waste bins. Photography is generally allowed in open areas, but always follow current regulations. Plan at least half a day if visiting nearby attractions as well. Why Visit Zoological Garden Alipore? The Zoological Garden Alipore is much more than a zoo—it is a historic institution that blends wildlife conservation, education, and recreation. Its century-old heritage, diverse collection of animals, lush green surroundings, and central location make it one of Kolkata’s most rewarding attractions for families, students, photographers, and wildlife enthusiasts. A visit offers both a relaxing escape into nature and an opportunity to learn about the importance of protecting biodiversity. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. Why is the Zoological Garden Alipore famous? It is India’s oldest officially established zoological garden and is renowned for its rich collection of wildlife, conservation programs, and the legendary Aldabra giant tortoise Adwaita. 2. Is Alipore Zoo and Zoological Garden Alipore the same? Yes. “Alipore Zoo” is the popular name for the official Zoological Garden Alipore. 3. What are the opening hours of Alipore Zoo? The zoo is generally open from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM and remains closed on Wednesdays. 4. What is the entry fee for the Zoological Garden Alipore? The standard ticket is approximately ₹30 for adults and ₹10 for children, though charges may change. 5. Which animals are the main attractions? Royal Bengal Tigers, White Tigers, Lions, Giraffes, Rhinoceroses, Hippopotamuses, Chimpanzees, Crocodiles, and numerous exotic birds. 6. How much time is needed to visit the zoo? Most visitors spend between 2 and 4 hours exploring the zoo. 7. What is the best season to visit? October to March is considered the best time due to pleasant weather. 8. Is photography allowed? Photography is generally permitted for personal use, subject to prevailing zoo regulations and any applicable camera fees. 9. Is the zoo suitable for children? Yes. It is one of Kolkata’s most popular family attractions and offers an educational experience for children. 10. Which metro station is nearest to the zoo? Majerhat (Purple Line) and Jatin Das Park (Blue Line) are among the nearest metro stations. 11. Is parking available? Yes, parking facilities are available near the entrance, though availability may be limited during peak seasons. 12. Can I combine the zoo with other attractions? Yes. Many visitors combine it with the Victoria Memorial, St. Paul’s Cathedral, Maidan, National Library, Birla Planetarium, and Alipore Museum in a single sightseeing itinerary. 13. Is food available inside the zoo? There are food kiosks and refreshment counters inside or near the zoo premises, though options may vary. 14. Is the zoo wheelchair accessible? Many areas are accessible, but some older pathways may present challenges. Visitors requiring assistance should check current accessibility arrangements before visiting. 15. Is Zoological Garden Alipore worth visiting? Absolutely. With its historic significance, extensive animal collection, conservation efforts, and beautiful landscaped grounds, it remains one of the top places to visit in Kolkata for visitors of all ages.
